title: Developer audit hooks for structured tool calls PRD (draft)
summary: Draft PRD proposing a lightweight, developer-facing audit hook system for Hosted API structured tool calls. The feature adds SDK and runtime primitives to capture verifiable metadata about tool invocations, partial/streamed structured outputs, and client-side assertions so teams can debug regressions and meet compliance needs without sacrificing low-latency streaming UX.
problem_statement: Teams building tool-enabled experiences with streaming responses face two recurring issues: (1) opaque tool call provenance when outputs are partially streamed or transformed by client adaptors, which complicates debugging and post-hoc analysis; (2) difficulty tying model/response regressions to changes in prompt, model variant, or tool runtime because telemetry is fragmented across SDKs and backend. Current traces capture tokens and latencies but not a compact, verifiable audit trail for structured tool outputs that can be retained cheaply and queried by engineers and compliance teams.
user_personas: Product engineer integrating tool calls and streaming into a chat UI; needs fast local replay and clear failure attribution
ML engineer running evals and rollouts; needs deterministic hooks to reproduce a quality regression tied to a model variant
Platform/Compliance engineer auditing production tool calls for data governance and incident postmortems
Solutions engineer triaging a customer issue where a partial streamed output triggered incorrect downstream automation
goals: Provide an opt-in, low-bandwidth audit envelope for each tool call and structured output frame that can be sampled/retained at route-level granularity
Make the audit envelope verifiable and machine-friendly (compact JSON schema + signature or hash) so clients and operators can link artifacts deterministically
Expose ergonomic SDK primitives to collect, enrich, and locally replay audit records without blocking streaming latency budgets
Integrate audit records with Console trace views and Optimize evaluations so regressions can be correlated with prompt sets, model variants, and quantization profiles
non_goals: Provide full content archiving for all streaming tokens (we will rely on sampling and optional retention tiers)
Replace existing audit/compliance product offerings — this is a developer-facing runtime trace improvement, not a legal evidence store
Force synchronous verification that would add noticeable tail latency to streaming responses
solution_overview: Introduce a compact audit envelope emitted for each structured tool call or transactional output frame. The envelope includes: route id, session id (opaque), timestamp, model variant, tool identifier, tool-call-id (UUID), output-frame-id, a small canonicalization hash of the structured payload (or first N bytes for very large payloads), a minimal event type (invocation|partial|complete|retry|error), and optional developer-supplied tags. The runtime attaches a short HMAC (service-side) when retention is enabled so offline consumers can verify envelope authenticity. SDKs will expose a non-blocking listener API to capture envelopes and rehydrate them for local replay and annotated logs. Console will surface an 'audit trail' pane that groups envelopes by tool-call-id and correlates them with traces and cost/latency metrics.
api_contract_examples:
Example: HTTP/JSON response stream element (newline-delimited) with audit envelope

{
  "type": "audit-envelope",
  "envelope": {
    "route_id": "r-01G7...",
    "session_id": "s-58a2...",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-15T14:22:08Z",
    "model": "redwood-v2-small",
    "tool_id": "web_search:v1",
    "tool_call_id": "tc-3f2e...",
    "frame_id": "f-0001",
    "event": "partial",
    "payload_hash": "sha256:4b2f...",
    "hmac": "hmac-sha256:abc123..."
  }
}

Notes: the envelope element is intentionally small; structured payloads continue to stream as separate elements (type=structured-frame). Clients can choose to persist envelopes only, or envelopes + payload fragments for short windows. Envelopes are valid JSON and can be recorded in logging systems without parsing costs.
streaming_behavior_summary:
- Envelopes are interleaved into the streaming output as dedicated events. They do not replace or modify structured-frame events.
- Emission policy: for every tool invocation, emit a 'invocation' envelope; for long-running outputs emit 'partial' envelopes at configurable intervals (default every 1–2s or every NKB of payload), and a 'complete' envelope when the tool finishes.
- Backpressure: SDK listener APIs must be non-blocking; envelopes are best-effort for local SDK consumers. The runtime always delivers envelopes to Console/telemetry; client-side capture is advisory to avoid increasing tail latency.
- Sampling: retention and export can be configured at route, team, or customer level. By default, sample 1% of invocations, with a route-level override for higher-sampled routes (e.g., canary).
sdk_ergonomics_changes: Add AuditListener interface with callbacks on_envelope(envelope) and on_frame(frame_meta) — non-blocking and async
Provide a small helper to compute payload_hash locally using canonicalization rules shipped in SDK (ensures parity with runtime hash)
Offer a persisted 'mini-log' writer helper which rotates and encrypts envelope logs for offline replay and incident attachments
Expose opt-in config on the client: audit_sampling_rate, local_retention_window_seconds, persist_envelopes=true|false
Default SDK behavior: no envelope capture unless route-level policy or explicit SDK opt-in to avoid accidental data exfiltration
telemetry_and_observability: Console: new Audit Trail pane + table grouped by tool_call_id with filters for model, event type, timeframe
Trace linkage: Zipkin/OTEL spans annotated with tool_call_id and frame_id for correlation
Metrics: per-route audit envelope emission rate, envelope delivery latency, envelope HMAC verification failures
Logs: sampled envelopes exported to BigQuery/Clickhouse for ad-hoc queries and eval correlation
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (experiment) — internal dogfood only: SDK support + Console panel for internal routes (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (alpha) — enable envelopes for customers in a gated program; default sample rate 1%; collect feedback on envelope shape and SDK ergonomics (4 weeks)
Phase 2 (beta) — add route-level controls in Console, HMAC verification option, and persisted export to analytics storage (6 weeks)
Phase 3 (general availability) — public SDK docs, sample code, retention tiers, SLA guidance for audit exports
success_metrics: Time-to-root-cause for tool-related production incidents reduced by 30% for participating routes
Number of support tickets requiring memory-span reproduction (logs only) falls by 25%
Adoption: 15% of active hosted-api routes opt into <1 month after GA for higher sampling
Mean envelope delivery latency (runtime->console) < 250ms for 95th percentile
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Envelopes could leak PII if payload hashes are reversible or if devs attach full payloads locally. Mitigation: default to hashes only, SDK explicit opt-in to save payload fragments, and provide canonical redact helpers.
Risk: Increased telemetry volume and cost. Mitigation: sampling defaults, route-level overrides, and retention tiers to control storage costs.
Risk: HMAC keys and signature handling increases complexity for private deployments. Mitigation: make HMAC optional and provide integration docs for customer KMS use in Private mode.
open_questions: Canonicalization: what exact canonical JSON rules do we require for payload_hash across languages? (affects cross-SDK verification)
HMAC key rotation UX for Private: how will we surface key rotation to on-prem control planes?
Sampling semantics: should sampling be decision-time (runtime decides per invocation) or post-hoc (store all envelopes short-term and drop later)?
Regulatory: do we need an explicit 'legal hold' signal that pins certain envelopes from sampling/discarding?
notes_to_engineering: Implementation should aim for minimal allocations on the hot path. Envelopes must be constructed from existing request/response metadata where possible to avoid additional lookups. Provide a small language-agnostic spec (1–2 pages) for envelope canonicalization and verification that SDK teams can implement. Expect a small feature flag coupling in runtime to avoid extra JSON generation for routes with no audit enabled.
